record.title: GEPA-Curator reports better agent prompt optimization by filtering noisy feedback and retrieving past successes
record.summary: A preprint introduces GEPA-Curator, which curates task rollouts before reflective prompt updates and retrieves prior successful trajectories as reference context. The authors report better held-out results than GEPA/ACE across WebArena, ALFWorld, AppWorld and τ-bench, using Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview or Claude Opus 5 as optimizer models and gpt-oss-120B as actor. Across four WebArena domains, the reported aggregate is 82.1% vs 78.7% for GEPA with Gemini and 84.5% vs 79.5% with Opus. On four additional test sets, reported average gains over GEPA/ACE range from 5.0 to 14.3 percentage points with Gemini and 8.1 to 12.6 points with Opus. These are author-reported benchmark results from manually seeded prompt optimization; they do not establish open-ended goal discovery, persistent weight improvement or general autonomous self-improvement.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: GEPA-Curator selects task experiences and retrieves prior successful trajectories to provide cleaner context to a reflective prompt optimizer.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report higher held-out WebArena aggregate success for GEPA-Curator than GEPA with both Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and Claude Opus 5 optimizer models.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report mean held-out gains over GEPA and ACE on ALFWorld, AppWorld and tau-bench in their tested configurations.

claims.label: INFERRED
claims.text: The results establish general autonomous self-improvement or persistent model-weight improvement.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction has verified the reported held-out gains, task curation decisions or cost accounting.
The results do not establish transfer to unseen task families or quantify persistent prompt-regression risk after mutations.
Meta-Harness-Curator results use one optimization run per setting.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported gains hold, filtering noisy agent feedback and grounding prompt revisions in prior successes could improve measured agent optimization across several benchmark families. This is consequential to self-improvement methodology but remains limited to manually seeded benchmark tasks and does not demonstrate open-ended or weight-level recursive improvement.
limitations: One author-reported preprint with no independent reproduction located.

Main experiments optimize manually written seed prompts on benchmark task sets; they do not test open-ended goal or target selection, model-weight updates or broad transfer outside the evaluated tasks.
Held-out sets are part of benchmark-specific optimization and final model selection uses validation scores; no independent confirmation distribution beyond those benchmark test splits is reported.
The Meta-Harness extension uses one optimization run per method and setting, so run-to-run variance is unknown there.
Evaluator, environment and task-diagnosis errors remain possible; the paper itself reports some task diagnoses later reversed.
brief.summary: A preprint introduces GEPA-Curator, which curates task rollouts before reflective prompt updates and retrieves prior successful trajectories as reference context. The authors report better held-out results than GEPA/ACE across WebArena, ALFWorld, AppWorld and τ-bench, using Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview or Claude Opus 5 as optimizer models and gpt-oss-120B as actor. Across four WebArena domains, the reported aggregate is 82.1% vs 78.7% for GEPA with Gemini and 84.5% vs 79.5% with Opus. On four additional test sets, reported average gains over GEPA/ACE range from 5.0 to 14.3 percentage points with Gemini and 8.1 to 12.6 points with Opus. These are author-reported benchmark results from manually seeded prompt optimization; they do not establish open-ended goal discovery, persistent weight improvement or general autonomous self-improvement.

technical.claimed_result: The authors argue that curated rollouts provide cleaner learning signals and improve prompt mutation quality across optimizer models and agent benchmarks. The reported results remain author-run preprint evidence.
technical.compute_or_cost: The authors report an Efficient GEPA-Curator variant with 1.31x total optimization cost versus GEPA alongside benchmark gains; on non-WebArena benchmarks it reports $173.98 versus $768.69 for ACE, using a relatively cheap actor. Cost figures are author-reported and exclude specified final tests/WebArena hosting.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public preprint reports mean held-out WebArena success of 82.1% for GEPA-Curator versus 78.7% for GEPA with Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, and 84.5% versus 79.5% with Claude Opus 5, across four websites. On ALFWorld, AppWorld Test-N/Test-C and tau-bench, the authors report mean gains over GEPA of 14.3 percentage points with Gemini and 8.1 points with Opus; reported gains over ACE are 5.0 and 12.6 points respectively. A GitLab ablation reports 88.6% for the combined curator, versus 82.8% for GEPA without Pareto selection, with task curation and success retrieval individually at 84.2% and 84.7%.
technical.implementation_status: Research preprint with described method and author-reported experiments; code availability and independent reproduction were not verified in this activation.
technical.mechanism: A Curator maintains task histories and selects a minibatch likely to provide useful reflection signal, temporarily skipping tasks with repeated stable success, likely environment/harness failures or inconsistent evaluation. For failed tasks it may retrieve a prior successful trajectory as a concrete contrastive reference. The existing reflective prompt optimizer then produces the mutation; the Curator adds context and task selection rather than changing the optimizer itself.
technical.novelty: Explicitly curates which task histories and prior successes should guide reflective prompt optimization, addressing noisy attribution from tool, harness, environment and evaluator failures.
technical.regime: Prompt optimization on GoBrowse/WebArena, ALFWorld, AppWorld and tau-bench benchmark tasks. Main experiments use manually written seed prompts, gpt-oss-120B actor, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview or Claude Opus 5 optimizer and held-out test splits. The separate Meta-Harness extension uses coding-agent harness optimization.
technical.reproducibility: The preprint describes task splits, rollout budgets, repeated runs for the main prompt experiments and some ablations, but results are not independently reproduced. The Meta-Harness extension uses one optimization run per method and setting, with three samples per test task.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares against GEPA and ACE using the same seed prompt, evaluator, action limits and environment configuration for the main WebArena setup; it also reports benchmark-specific split and rollout budgets.

brief.title: GEPA-Curator reports better agent prompt optimization by filtering noisy feedback and retrieving past successes
brief.why_it_matters: The paper isolates a concrete failure mode in experience-driven agent improvement: execution failures may come from the prompt, harness, environment or evaluator, so treating every failure as useful learning signal can damage later behavior. In the tested benchmark regime, selecting cleaner task histories and supplying past successes improved reported held-out prompt performance. This is useful evidence for designing self-improvement loops, while leaving independent reproduction and broad transfer unresolved.
